text:
Calgary lost Kevin Bahl for the season this month, and the headlines since have been about who replaces him: The Hockey Writers floated a trade for a former top-10 pick, and others wondered how far the AHL depth can stretch. Bahl and Simon Nemec had been one of the two pairs Ryan Huska leaned on most, so the defense that was already thin got thinner.

The happier story is Zayne Parekh. Daily Faceoff wrote that he is blossoming into a star, and the power play runs through him. And the goaltending has kept things afloat: Dustin Wolf stole a win in Los Angeles that Sportsnet compared to a Jonathan Quick game, and Devin Cooley has been a feature story of his own at NHL.com.

The underlying team is the concern. The Flames get 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 46% at five on five, and only 43% over the last ten games. Their power play produces 0.36 expected goals a game, which is thin for a team that needs goals. At 10-11-1 they have one more point than our expected points say they've earned, and our odds put them at 12% to make the playoffs. Watch whether the goalies can keep covering for a team that spends most nights in its own end.
